Om arbeidsgiveren:
OM OSS
Vi er Ola og Lars Berbusmel, to brødre med en ekte lidenskap for mat. Ola er bakeren, og Lars er kokken. Vi vokste opp med pappas fisketurer, mammas hjemmebakte brød, mormors fantastiske fiskegrateng og bestefars bløtkaker.

Vår filosofi er enkel: Vi elsker lokale retter og råvarer, rene smaker og å mikse tradisjonelle og moderne teknikker.

For oss er lokal mat en hjertesak. Vi tror på at kortreist mat smaker bedre og samtidig gir noe tilbake til lokalsamfunnet. Derfor samarbeider vi med lokale produsenter for å sikre ferske, bærekraftige råvarer – og for å være med på å bevare og utvikle de tradisjonene vi er så glade i.
BAKERI OG DELIKATESSE
Høsten 2018 åpnet vi vårt eget håndverksbakeri med kafé og delikatessebutikk midt på torget i Bodø. Det er et koselig sted hvor du kan ta en kopp kaffe, holde lunsjmøter eller kjøpe noe ekstra godt til helgen.

Vi legger sjela i håndverket vårt, med fokus på kvalitet og lokale råvarer. Brødene våre bakes med få, men nøye utvalgte ingredienser, og får god tid til å heve – for vi vet at gode ting tar tid.

I delikatesseavdelingen vår finner du produkter vi selv elsker å bruke – fra spekemat og oster til oljer, eddiker og ferskt kjøtt. Vi plukker ut det beste for å gjøre måltidene dine ekstra spesielle.
CATERING
Vi leverer catering til både små og store anledninger. Enten det er bryllup, dåp, konfirmasjon, møter og eventer, en tapaskveld med vennegjengen eller møtemat på jobben, har vi noe for deg.

Våre menyer gjenspeiler sesongen og det vi mener er best akkurat nå. Alt er laget fra bunnen av, med lokale råvarer og leverandører der det er mulig.

jobs.occupation: Researcher in Biostatistics
jobs.description:
About the position
We are seeking applicants with a strong methodological background in biostatistics and causal inference for a 3-year 20% researcher position in Biostatistics, in a project on causal inference for effects of health related interventions on working life outcomes, at the Oslo Centre for Biostatistics and Epidemiology (OCBE), Department of Biostatistics, University of Oslo (UiO).
 
OCBE is one of Europe's most active biostatistics groups with currently about 80 researchers. OCBE is internationally recognized, with interests spanning a broad range of areas, including causal inference and time-to-event analysis, clinical trials, epidemiology, high dimensional statistics, infectious disease, machine learning and mathematical modelling. The centre has numerous collaborations with leading biomedical research groups internationally and in Norway.
More about the position
The candidate will be part of the research group on causal inference and survival analysis led by professor Jon Michael Gran, where they will work on causal inference with applications to longitudinal data from large population-wide registries. The position is connected to the project “Improving causal inference for individual working life trajectories from registry data: studying interventions, estimands and heterogeneity”, funded by the Research Council of Norway (RCN). The project is a close collaboration with research groups at the National Institute of Occupational Health (STAMI) and Oslo University Hospital (OUS).

The candidate will pursue research on causal inference for treatment effect estimation from complex longitudinal data, collected from various population wide registries. An emphasis will be made on exposure measurement error, interference, effect heterogeneity and the analysis of individual outcome trajectories. However, other methods may also be relevant. Methods should be motivated in and applied to answering the subject matter research questions of the overall project, such as of the effects of interventions for a more inclusive working life (including rehabilitation measures and work place facilitation) or the effects of sustained medical treatments (including use of opioids and other type of pain treatment for patients after traumatic injury). Outcomes of interest will be related to long term health, sick leave and work participation. 

The candidate’s role in the project will be both to supervise other project members and to conduct own methodological and applied research in biostatistics. We provide an exciting and friendly research environment for the development and application of new methods in a collaborative and interdisciplinary fashion, with various national and international collaborators. The candidate will work closely with other project members at OCBE, STAMI and OUS, other external collaborators, and the causal inference and survival analysis group at OCBE. The candidate will participate in regular project meetings and must have the ability to work well in a multi-disciplinary team.

The candidate’s workplace will be at OCBE’s premises in the UiO building Domus Medica.

Preferred starting date for the position is January 1st, 2027. 
Qualifications requirements

• Applicants must hold a degree corresponding to a Norwegian doctoral degree in biostatistics or statistics.

• Strong quantitative and computational skills is required. Applicants should be fluent in R or equivalent software.

jobs.description:
The Departments of Solar Power Systems and Energy System Analysis at the Institute for Energy Technology (IFE) have a vacant PhD research fellowship focused on modelling how increasing photovoltaic (PV) generation affects Norwegian power grids. The position is part of the KSP project Solvar and the Norwegian PV Research Centre (FME SOLAR) and combines regional PV production modelling with power system analysis to support safe and cost-effective integration of solar power. 

The Departments of Solar Power Systems and Energy System Analysis at IFE conduct research on PV systems analysis (including performance and forecasting of PV plants), and energy system modelling (including techno-economic modelling and power flow analysis). The candidate will be supervised by a team of researchers from IFE and the University of Oslo with strong competence in the generation and distribution of electricity. The PhD will be affiliated with the Department of Technology Systems at the University of Oslo.

The PhD candidate will work on robust power grids and regional PV production profiles. The results will help grid operators assess hosting capacity, operational risks and suitable measures for integrating more PV. The work will combine physical grid and PV modelling, data analysis and selected data-driven methods. Regional PV profiles may be investigated for spatial scales ranging from individual transformers and feeders to larger regions. Validation will use measured and historical PV data, irradiance data, building information and grid data made available through the project and open data sources.   In addition to being integrated into internationally leading research groups at IFE, the candidate will have the opportunity to collaborate with other world-class research communities, e.g., through the International Energy Agency’s Photovoltaic Power Systems Programme Task 16 & 19, and through contributions to the Pan-European Climate Database. jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
We invite applications for a 3-year PhD Candidate position on the future role of hydrogen and hydrogen products in industrial decarbonization. The position is based at the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management, located at NTNU’s campus in Trondheim.

The mission of Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management (IØT) is to carry out education, research, and innovation activities at an international level at the intersection between technology/natural sciences and business economics, management, and HSE. The department’s activities aim to contribute to sustainable value creation within technology-based areas in industry, business, and the public sector in Norway

 

About the position

Electrification is widely promoted as a key pathway to industrial decarbonization. At the same time, hydrogen and carbon capture and storage (CCS) are increasingly recognized as important solutions for sectors where direct electrification may be difficult or uneconomic. This has led to a growing debate about the future role of "electrons versus molecules" in a net-zero economy.

Most existing studies assume that today's industrial structure remains largely unchanged and focus on how current industries can reduce emissions. However, deep decarbonization may fundamentally reshape industrial production, value chains, competitiveness, and the location of energy-intensive activities. As a result, future hydrogen demand may depend as much on industrial transformation as on technological choices.

This PhD project will investigate how alternative pathways toward a zero-emission industrial sector affect the future demand for hydrogen and the development of hydrogen value chains. The research will analyze the interplay between electrification, hydrogen, and CCS, while explicitly accounting for potential changes in industrial structures and production systems.

 

The project addresses research questions like:

• How will future hydrogen demand vary across alternative industrial decarbonization pathways?
• Which industrial sectors are likely to rely on electrification, hydrogen, or CCS to achieve net-zero emissions?
• How might industrial transformation affect hydrogen production, transport, storage, and trade?
• What level of hydrogen deployment is required to justify dedicated hydrogen infrastructure and markets?
• How can Europe and Norway prepare for different industrial and energy-system transition pathways?
 

The successful candidate will develop and analyze future scenarios for industrial transformation, hydrogen demand, and infrastructure development. The project will contribute to the scientific and policy debate on how competitive zero-emission industries can emerge under different transition strategies.
Research environment
The PhD candidate will join a multidisciplinary research environment at the intersection of energy economics, industrial economics, operations research, and energy systems analysis.

The position is affiliated with FME HYDROGENi, the Norwegian Research and Innovation Centre for Hydrogen and Ammonia. The centre brings together 46 research and industry partners to develop the knowledge, technologies, and solutions needed to support a sustainable hydrogen economy and contribute to Norway's ambitions for climate neutrality and industrial transformation. FME HYDROGENi conducts research across the hydrogen value chain, including hydrogen production, transport and storage, industrial and maritime applications, safety, and the broader role of hydrogen in future energy systems. The centre is funded by the Research Council of Norway through the Centres for Environment-friendly Energy Research (FME) programme and operates during the period 2022-2030

The PhD candidate will be hosted at the Managerial Economics, Finance and Operations Research (BEDØK) group at the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management. The group is one of Norway’s leading academic environments in operations research, logistics, optimization, and quantitative decision support. The candidate will work in close collaboration with researchers from NTNU’s Department of Computer Science and Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Your role in the project
The PhD candidate will:

• Conduct original scientific research on hydrogen and industrial decarbonization pathways.
• Develop and analyze scenarios for industrial transformation and climate neutrality.
• Assess the future role of electrification, hydrogen, and CCS across industrial sectors.
• Quantify hydrogen demand and infrastructure requirements under alternative transition pathways.
• Publish research results in leading international journals and conferences.
• Collaborate with academic, industry, and public-sector partners.
• Complete the required coursework as part of the PhD programme.
• Contribute to dissemination and communication of research findings.
 

Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Qualification requirements
Applicants must hold a master’s degree in a relevant field with strong academic results (B or better according to NTNU’s grading scale). Relevant academic backgrounds include:

• Operations research or optimization
• Energy systems
• Energy Economics
• Engineering disciplines with strong quantitative and analytical content
• Or other closely related disciplines.
Applicants must demonstrate strong analytical and quantitative skills.

The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Desired qualifications
The following qualifications will be considered an advantage:

• Experience with energy system modelling, scenario analysis, or techno-economic analysis.
• Knowledge of hydrogen technologies, industrial decarbonization, or climate policy.
• Experience with quantitative modelling and data analysis.
• Programming skills in Python, Julia, R, GAMS, or similar tools.
• Interest in interdisciplinary research at the interface of technology, economics, and policy.
Applicants in the final phase of their master’s studies are encouraged to apply.
Personal characteristics
We are looking for a candidate who:

• Is intellectually curious and motivated to conduct high-quality research
• Has strong analytical and problem-solving skills
• Works independently and in a structured manner
• Has excellent communication and collaboration skills
• Thrives in an interdisciplinary research environment. 
• Is interested in research with relevance for industry, policy, and society.
Emphasis will be placed on scientific quality, research potential, and personal suitability.
We offer
• An exciting and international academic environment with opportunities for competence development 
• Close collaboration with leading researchers in energy systems modelling, optimization, and something else

• Participation in research addressing key challenges of the green transition.
• Opportunities for international research stays and conference participation.
• An open and inclusive workplace  with engaged colleagues

Information about working and living in Norway can be found at the following link: https://www.workinnorway.no/en/Home
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is connected to the PhD program at the Faculty of Economics and Management, and the faculty will be your employer. Appointment to a PhD position requires that you are admitted to the PhD programme in Industrial Economics and Technology Management within three months of employment, and that you participate in an organized PhD programme during the employment period.

Trondheim is the workplace. For necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.Any statutory leave will be added to the employment period.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important to stay updated on professional and organizational changes and adapt to these.

The plan should reflect the applicant’s research interests and provide an outline of how they envision contributing to the project objectives.

If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both bachelor's and master's education, in addition to other higher education. In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential for research will also count in the assessment of the candidates.  

NTNU is committed to following the evaluation criteria for research quality according to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment – DORA and the commitments in CoARA (responsible research assessment and recognition of a broader range of academic contributions in line with NTNU's societal mission).

Incomplete applications will not be considered.
General information
A public applicant list with names, ages, job titles, and municipalities of residence will be prepared after the application deadline. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted.

Furthermore, Trondheim offers excellent educational opportunities (including international schools) and opportunities to enjoy nature, culture, and family life, with low crime rates and clean air quality.

Questions about the position can be directed to Professor Asgeir Tomasgard (asgeir.tomasgard @ntnu.no) or Professor Anne Neumann (anne.neumann@ntnu.no).

The main objective of CHARM MSCA Doctoral Network project is to develop new sustainable conservation and restoration solutions, adapted to the current and future climate conditions, designed in a circular economy philosophy, having a low environmental footprint and high handprint. CHARM also responds to socio-economical requirements of wellbeing and proposes conservation/restoration solutions economically acceptable and respecting the cultural value of buildings.

CHARM proposes a holistic approach including:

• Site observation and data collection
• Data preparation to be used by AI, models, etc
• Methods for understanding and modelling past and future degradation of architectural heritage
• Sustainable conservation solutions to several observed problems
• Assessment of the impact of architectural conservation on the environment and of the environment (past, present and future) on architectural heritage
• Bidirectional interactions with society proposing risk management plans but also taking into account the society wills and needs
The vision of CHARM MSCA project is to educate young and talented scientists towards a combined high-level experimental and data driven approach for the early-stage accurate, precise detection of hydro-climate impact on cultural heritage, to answer to recruitment needs in time of climate change and natural hazards impact about research and innovation in the sector of cultural heritage conservation and restoration. 

CHARM network gathers excellent academic centers that have decennial experience in the field of risk assessment, adaptation and mitigation solutions to the climate change impact, conservation of cultural heritage and restoration, documented by scientific papers published in high impact-factor journals, and by previous EU funded research projects. CHARM puts together researchers from universities and research organisms, national and local organizations in charge of Cultural Heritage conservation, Small and Midsize Enterprises, industrial producer of building materials, and Non-Governmental Organization, from 9 European and 1 South American countries.
Description of DC2 PhD position
Project title: Understanding conservation condition and rehabilitation needs at district scale in time of energy saving and climate change via machine learning driven method

Topic in brief:

The aim is to implement an approach based on artificial intelligence (AI) in the form of CNN to automatically detect cracks and morphological indices in order to manage the large amount of data obtained from photogrammetry and earth observations images.

Objectives:

This doctoral project aims to develop deep learning neural networks to investigate data in available database (e.g., EU building stock observatory and other similar database) to:

• classify building stock at district scale more prone to decay based on buildings construction year, location, main constitutive material, exposure, use and
• to predict potential maintenance and restoration priority based on (i) and existing energy retrofit directive and/or risk maps 
Expected results:

(i)to build high-quality dataset highlighting the façade that is more prone to decay at district/city level from existing raw database; 

(ii) to apply deep learning neural networks (e.g., convolutional neural network) to perform semi-automatic decay pattern segmentation and associated mapping; 

(iii) to correlate the maintenance of buildings at district/city level with decay patterns/features at district scale to prioritize large scale intervention; and 

(iv) to optimize the maintenance activities by leveraging these correlations learned by machine-learning based approaches.

We are seeking a researcher with a background in welding, metal additive manufacturing or a related area of physical metallurgy for an approximately one-year position within SFI PhysMet (Centre for Sustainable and Competitive Metallurgical and Manufacturing Industry; www.ntnu.edu/physmet) at the Department of Materials Science and Engineering, NTNU.

The position offers the opportunity to take a leading role in an experimental study of low transformation temperature (LTT) alloys. You will build on existing specimens and recent results, shape the remaining investigations and lead the preparation of a full-length journal manuscript together with the project team. We welcome applicants who enjoy connecting microstructural observations with physical metallurgy understanding and transforming experimental findings into clear scientific conclusions.

Your immediate leader is Head of Department.
About the job
LTT alloys undergo transformation from austenite to martensite at relatively low temperatures. The associated volume expansion can counteract thermal contraction and offers a route to managing residual stresses in welding and additive manufacturing. Understanding how processing conditions and repeated thermal cycles affect their microstructure is important for assessing their potential in these applications.

The experimental work has so far focused on directed energy deposition (DED). Single tracks, double tracks and small cuboids have been printed from three LTT alloys. Initial characterisation has included sectioning and light optical microscopy (LOM) to examine printing defects and dilution, Vickers hardness measurements, and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) on selected specimens, including reconstruction of prior-austenite grains.

More recently, cubes have also been produced by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) using two of the alloy powders. Microstructural characterisation of these specimens by LOM is currently in progress.

You will bring the existing and emerging results together to investigate the relationships between processing, microstructure, printing quality and hardness. The work will include identifying the most valuable scientific questions, establishing where the DED and LPBF results can be meaningfully compared, and completing focused complementary characterisation. The main outcome should be one or more full-length manuscripts prepared and submitted to a relevant peer-reviewed journal.
Duties of the position
One of the main objectives of SFI PhysMet is to explore and develop innovative processing and joining methods with enhanced sustainability and competitiveness. You will contribute to this aim through the following activities:

• Review, consolidate and document the existing specimens, processing information and characterisation results.
• Define a focused plan for completing the study, identifying the additional analyses or experiments needed to support its scientific conclusions.
• Carry out and analyse complementary microstructural characterisation and strength property  measurements in collaboration with the project team.
• Investigate the effects of alloy composition, processing conditions, dilution and repeated thermal cycles on microstructure and hardness, using the available evidence.
• Develop a scientifically justified comparison of the DED and LPBF results for the alloys studied by both processes.
• Lead the interpretation of the results and the preparation and submission of at least one full-length journal manuscript in collaboration with the project team.
• Communicate the findings through project meetings and relevant scientific conferences and document the data and analysis procedures for future use.
You will work closely with colleagues and partners within SFI PhysMet. Research visits and participation in relevant conferences are encouraged as opportunities to strengthen the study, exchange knowledge and expand your scientific network.
Required selection criteria
• A PhD in materials science and engineering, metallurgy, welding technology, mechanical engineering or a closely related discipline, or documented scientific qualifications at an equivalent level.
• Relevant experimental research experience in welding metallurgy, metal additive manufacturing or a related field involving solidification and phase transformations in metallic materials.
• Hands-on experience with metallographic sample preparation and microstructural characterisation of metallic materials, by light optical and electron microscopy methods.
• Demonstrated ability to analyse experimental data independently and relate processing conditions, microstructure and material properties.
• Experience in scientific writing, demonstrated by relevant publications, and the ability to take a leading role in manuscript preparation.
• Excellent written and oral English communication skills.Preferred selection criteria

• Experience with DED and/or LPBF, including interpretation of processing parameters and thermal histories.

• Experience acquiring and/or analysing EBSD data, particularly reconstruction of prior-austenite grains.

jobs.description:
Chef Wanted for Sommarøy - Seasonal Position with Possibility of Extension
Would you like to work as a chef in the beautiful surroundings of Sommarøy, just outside Tromsø? We are currently looking for a skilled and dedicated chef to join our team at Sommarøy Hotel for an exciting seasonal position.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a kitchen, takes pride in using quality ingredients, and would love to combine work with unforgettable nature experiences in Northern Norway.

The position is full-time (100%), starting in November and running until the end of March, with the possibility of extension.
Job Responsibilities
• Preparing and presenting dinner dishes and à la carte meals.
• Ensuring high standards of food quality and presentation.
• Contributing to the efficient and well-organised daily operation of the kitchen.
• Maintaining high standards of hygiene and following food safety procedures, including HACCP.
• Working closely with the kitchen team and other departments.
• Contributing to a positive working environment and excellent guest experiences.Qualifications
• Experience as a chef in a hotel, restaurant, or similar establishment.
• Experience with à la carte service.
• A professional chef qualification is preferred, but relevant work experience may compensate.
• Ability to work independently as well as part of a team.
• Good understanding of ingredients, food quality, and kitchen routines.
• Organised, flexible, and solution-oriented.
• Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment.
• Fluent in either Norwegian or English.What We Offer
• A full-time seasonal position from November until the end of March, with the possibility of extension.
• An exciting working environment surrounded by spectacular natural scenery.
• A friendly and international working environment.
• Staff accommodation available for only NOK 2,500 per month. You will have your own bedroom in a shared house with two other chefs.
• The opportunity to experience Northern Norway, with spectacular landscapes and the Northern Lights right on your doorstep.About Sommarøy Hotel
Sommarøy Hotel is situated in the scenic surroundings of Sommarøy, approximately a one-hour drive from Tromsø. Surrounded by the sea, mountains, and beautiful Northern Norwegian nature, the hotel attracts guests looking for unique experiences throughout the year.

Here, you will have the opportunity to become part of a kitchen team dedicated to creating memorable dining experiences for our guests.
Interested?
We would love to hear from you if you have kitchen experience and are ready for an exciting season on Sommarøy.

Please send us your application and CV as soon as possible. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis.

 

We look forward to hearing from you!

Sommarøy Hotel is a unique seaside hotel located on the beautiful island of Sommarøy, just one hour from Tromsø in Northern Norway. Surrounded by stunning Arctic nature, our hotel offers unforgettable experiences all year round, from the Northern Lights to the Midnight Sun. We are an international team passionate about great hospitality, quality food, and creating memorable experiences for our guests.
